criteria.description: Includes a model-card-style section stating intended use, capabilities, and EXPLICIT limitations of the AI — not just features.
Names out-of-scope or prohibited behaviours the assistant must not do (e.g. claims it can't substantiate, regulated content).
Specifies what data the capability needs, where it comes from, and addresses rights/privacy/consent and/or the feedback data captured to improve it.
Defines what 'good enough to ship' means and how quality will be measured offline and/or online — not just 'we'll track engagement'.
Makes an explicit approach decision (API model / fine-tune / own model, or RAG vs. fine-tune) with a rationale.
Addresses how users understand, verify, edit, or recover from the AI output (human-in-the-loop / trust).
Identifies AI-specific risks (failure, misuse) and any regulatory/compliance exposure with mitigations.
Success metrics include at least one quality measure plus a cost or latency guardrail that must not regress.
